contenido: Canon 1 If anyone has been castrated by doctors because of illness, or has been mutilated by barbarians, let him remain in the clergy. But if anyone, being healthy, has castrated himself, this holy synod commands that, if he is constituted in the clergy, he be excluded from the clergy, and that henceforth none of such be promoted. And just as this is clear regarding those who purposely do this and dare to mutilate themselves, so, on the contrary, if some have been castrated by barbarians or by their owners, and are otherwise found worthy, the rule admits such to the clergy.

Canon 2 Since many things have been done, either by necessity or by the importunity of men, outside the ecclesiastical rule, so that men who have recently come to the faith from the Gentile life, and catechized in a short time, are immediately taken to the spiritual laver, and as soon as they are baptized they are promoted to the episcopate or to the priesthood: it has seemed that nothing similar will be done from now on. Well, a lot of time is needed both for catechesis and, after baptism, for the test. The apostolic saying is written very clearly: "Not to the neophyte, lest, being arrogant, he fall into the judgment and snare of the devil." If over time any sin of the soul is found in the person, and it is convinced by two or three witnesses, such dismissal from the clergy. If anyone tries to do anything outside of this, as contumacious against the great synod, he will be in danger as regards the clergy.

Canon 3 The great synod completely prohibited that it is not lawful for the bishop, nor for the priest, nor for the deacon, nor for anyone at all who is in the clergy, to have with him an introduced woman, except perhaps the mother, or the sister, or the aunt, or only those persons who avoid suspicion.

Canon 4 It is appropriate that the bishop be ordained preferably by all the bishops in the province. If this is difficult, either due to urgent need, or due to the length of the path: at least three meeting there, and those absent also giving their vote and consent in writing, then the ordination is made. Confirmation of what is done in each province is attributed to the metropolitan bishop.

Those who say: "There was a time when he was not," and "before he was born he was not," and that he was made from nothing, or from another substance or essence, saying that the Son of God is created or convertible or mutable, these are anathematized by the Catholic and Apostolic Church.

Canon 6 Observe the ancient custom for Egypt, Libya and Pentapolis, so that the bishop of Alexandria has power over all of these: for also the bishop of the city of Rome has a similar custom. Likewise, also in Antioch and in the other provinces their privileges are preserved for the Churches. And let it be generally clear that if anyone is made a bishop without the opinion of the metropolitan, this great synod has defined that he should not be a bishop. But if, with the common and reasonable vote of all and according to the ecclesiastical canon, two or three contradict due to contentious pertinacity, the majority ruling prevails.
Canon 7 Since the custom and ancient tradition has prevailed that the bishop of Elia, that is, of Jerusalem, be honored: it has the consequence of honor, it saves the metropolitan dignity.

Canon 8 Concerning those who call themselves Cathars, that is, pure, when they ever approach the Catholic and Apostolic Church, it has seemed to the holy and great synod that, receiving the laying on of hands, they should thus remain in the clergy. First of all, it is advisable that they confess in writing that they will consent to and follow the dogmas of the Catholic and Apostolic Church: that is, that they will also commune with those we say and with those who fell in persecution, with respect to whom there is also an established time and a predetermined occasion; so that in everything they follow the dogmas of the Catholic Church. Wherever, whether in castles or cities, only those among them are ordained: those who are in the clergy remain in the same habit. But if, where there is a bishop of the Catholic Church, some of them approach: it is clear that the bishop of the Church will have the episcopal dignity; and he who is called bishop among them will have the honor of presbyter, unless the bishop pleases that he also share in the honor of the name. If this does not please him, he will provide the place of corebiscope or priest for the one who is in the clergy, so that it can be seen that he is completely in the clergy; so that there are not two bishops in the city.

Canon 9 If some have been promoted to priests without examination, or when they were examined they confessed their sins, and when they confessed them, men moved against the canon laid hands on them: the rule does not admit these. Well, it is typical of the Catholic Church to want to be irreproachable.

Canon 10 All those who have been ordained between the periods, either out of ignorance or knowing it by those who ordained: this does not prejudge the ecclesiastical canon. Well, acquaintances, they are deposed.

Canon 11 Concerning those who transgressed without necessity, or without loss of property, or without danger, or something similar to what is said at the time of the persecution of Licinius: it has seemed to the synod that, although they are lenient with them, they should not, however, be left without care. All, then, who truly do penance: let them be among the hearers for three years, and prostrate themselves for seven years; and for two years they commune with the people in prayer without the offering.

Canon 12 Those who, called by grace and having first shown their purpose, laying down the belts of the military, then returned like dogs to their vomit, so that some even gave money and restored themselves to military benefits: these, for ten years after the triennial time that is among the listeners, prostrate themselves. In all of these it is convenient to consider the purpose and type of penance. For as many as demonstrate conversion in fact and not in appearance, with fear, with tears, with patience and with good works: these, once the established time of hearing has elapsed, will already take communion among those who pray, and it will also be permissible for the bishop to establish something more human about them. But as many as acted with indifference and thought that the form of conversion was sufficient for entry into the church: these complied completely at all times.

Canon 13 Regarding those who leave this life, the ancient and canonical law will now also be kept: that if anyone leaves, he will not be defrauded of the last and necessary viaticum. If anyone, terminally ill and receiving communion, is found again among the living: let him be among those who communicate only by prayer. And in general, to everyone who goes out and asks to participate in the Eucharist, it is appropriate that the bishop offer it to them with examination.
Canon 14 Regarding catechumens and lapses, it has seemed to the holy and great synod that they are only three years among the listeners; then pray with the catechumens.

Canon 15 Because of the great disturbance and seditions that usually occur, it has seemed to completely eliminate the custom that, outside of the canonical form, has been found in some places: that neither the bishop, nor the priest, nor the deacon passes from one city to another. If anyone, after the definition of the holy and great synod, attempts something similar, or gives himself to such a thing: let the act be null and void, and let him be restored to the Church in which he was ordained bishop, or presbyter, or deacon.

Canon 16 All those who recklessly and without fear of God, and ignoring the ecclesiastical rule, have segregated themselves from the Church, whether priests, or deacons, or at all those counted in the canon: these must in no way be received into another Church; but every need must be applied to them so that they return to their parishes; or if they persevere, it is advisable to deprive them of communion. If anyone also dares to seize what belongs to another and ordain it in his Church, without the consent of the bishop from whom the one counted in the canon departed: let the ordination be void.

Canon 17 Since many counted in the canon, following greed and clumsy profits, have forgotten the divine Scripture that says: "He did not give his money at usury"; and, demanding interest, they demand a hundredfold: the holy and great synod has justly judged that if anyone, after this definition, is found receiving usury by negotiation, or negotiating in another way, or demanding hemioilas, or inventing anything similar at all for the sake of clumsy gain: he should be expelled from the clergy and remain outside the canon.

Canon 18 It has come to the holy and great synod that in some places and cities the deacons give the Eucharist to the priests: which neither the canon nor the custom has transmitted, that those who have no power to offer give the body of Christ to those who offer. It has also been known that some deacons already touch the Eucharist even before bishops. Therefore, let all these things be put away: and let the deacons remain in their measure, knowing that they are ministers of the bishops and inferior to the presbyters. Receive the Eucharist according to the order after the priests, the bishop or the priest. Nor is it lawful for deacons to sit among the priests. Well, it is against the canonical and out of order. If anyone does not want to obey even after these definitions: cessation of the diaconate.

Canon 19 Regarding the Paulianists who have taken refuge in the Catholic Church, it has been decided that they be completely rebaptized. If some in the past were numbered in the clergy: if they appear immaculate and blameless, rebaptized and ordained by the bishop of the Catholic Church. If the inquisition finds them inept: it is appropriate that they be deposed. Likewise also with respect to the deaconesses, and in general of those who are counted in the canon, the same form will be kept. We remember, however, the deaconesses who are in the habit, since they do not have any laying on of hands, so that they are counted entirely among the laity.

Canon 20 Since there are some who bend their knees on the Lord's Day, and on the days of Pentecost: so that everything may be observed in all the parishes, it has been decided by the holy synod that, standing, they should offer their vows to God.
